tests.name: jvm-jsonable-simple-roundtrip
tests.description: @jsonable toJson→fromJson roundtrip preserves primitive fields

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-fromjson-defaults
tests.description: @jsonable fromJson applies declared defaults for omitted keys

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-nested-object-fields
tests.description: @jsonable nested class fields serialize and deserialize recursively

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-array-fields
tests.description: @jsonable primitive array fields roundtrip element-wise

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-class-array-fields
tests.description: @jsonable arrays of nested class objects roundtrip through the nested fromJson/toJson

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-nullable-fields
tests.description: @jsonable nullable fields preserve explicit JSON null and non-null values

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-nullable-array-field
tests.description: @jsonable T[] | null field roundtrips both the null and the populated states

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-nullable-element-array-field
tests.description: @jsonable (int | null)[] field roundtrips value, null, and value elements in order

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-invalid-json-returns-null
tests.description: @jsonable fromJson returns the DEAL null for malformed JSON without throwing

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-extra-key-rejected
tests.description: @jsonable fromJson rejects extra keys by returning the DEAL null, not throwing

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-type-mismatch-failure
tests.description: @jsonable fromJson returns the DEAL null on field type mismatches (fractional int, out-of-safe-range int, wrong-typed string, non-object class value)

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-tojson-nan-error
tests.description: @jsonable toJson raises E8001 for a NaN number field (std/json.lua encode rejection)

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-non-jsonable-field-rejected
tests.description: a @jsonable class field of a class type without generated JSON functions is E4007, rejected before any backend

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-cross-module-roundtrip
tests.description: cross-module @jsonable helpers: imported fromJson/toJson calls and a nested field of imported class type with module-qualified nominal identity through a table-read boundary

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-cross-module-identity-failure
tests.description: a deserialized instance from another module carries its declaring module's nominal identity — a local same-name class read through a table boundary fails the nominal check with both module-qualified identities

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-optional-three-state
tests.description: @jsonable optional-nullable field preserves the three states exactly — missing omits the key, explicit null emits "field": null, and a value emits the value (spec §Optional-nullable roundtrip); has() reports presence

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-optional-default-and-write
tests.description: @jsonable optional field with a declared default starts present with that default (construction and fromJson), an assignment makes it present, and toJson emits the present default

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-table-field-roundtrip
tests.description: @jsonable table fields roundtrip JSON object values — nested objects become nested tables, and string-keyed reads cross the table boundary after fromJson

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-table-nested-arrays
tests.description: @jsonable table fields preserve nested JSON arrays: fromJson maps them to array-mode tables, toJson re-emits the identical array shape, and a table-typed read crosses the boundary

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-table-fromjson-non-object-rejected
tests.description: @jsonable fromJson accepts only a JSON object for a table field — an array, a number, and a string all fail validation with the DEAL null, never a throw

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-table-tojson-non-json-rejected
tests.description: @jsonable toJson raises E8001 for a table field holding a value outside the finite acyclic JSON-shaped set — a class instance is not a JSON leaf

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-cross-module-optional
tests.description: cross-module @jsonable optional fields: the imported helper deserializes into the DECLARING module's Missing-sentinel states — has() and nullable reads of the imported instance distinguish absent, present null, and present value across the module boundary

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-optional-nullable-class
tests.description: @jsonable optional-nullable nested class field preserves explicit null, value, and missing states — present null and nested values recurse through the nested fromJson/toJson helpers, the missing state omits the key

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-optional-table-rejected
tests.description: backend-rejection gate: an @jsonable class with an optional table field (`data?: table`) reads as `table | null` — a value shape the JVM slice keeps out of its typed positions — so the orchestrator reports E6000 and the rejected entry module writes no artifact, never an artifact javac rejects (the pre-fix emission stored the field as $T and later passed the Missing sentinel into that slot: javac 'incompatible types: Object cannot be converted to $T' after the CLI reported success)

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-deep-nesting-returns-null
tests.description: hostile deep nesting: ~20 KB of 20000 nested '[' ... ']' inside a table field returns the DEAL null — the emitted parser converts its StackOverflowError to the DEAL null exactly like LuaJIT's pcall(__json_parse, s), never an uncaught stack trace, exit 0

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-table-depth-guard
tests.description: bounded depth guard: 600 nested JSON objects inside a table field (past the emitted 512-level limit) are a validation failure — the table-value conversion's guard throws, the public C$fromJson wrapper converts the throw to the DEAL null, exit 0 (deterministic on any thread-stack size, unlike a StackOverflowError at the recursion limit)

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-unpaired-surrogate-returns-null
tests.description: unpaired UTF-16 surrogates: a lone high (0xD800) or lone low (0xDC00) surrogate decoded from a JSON backslash-u escape in a string field, and a lone surrogate in a table-field string leaf, are parse failures returning the DEAL null — the emitted parser scans every decoded JSON string with __hasUnpairedSurrogate exactly like LuaJIT's std/json.lua decoder error inside pcall(__json_parse, s), exit 0, never a throw

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-invalid-number-spellings-return-null
tests.description: invalid JSON number spellings: a leading zero (01, -01), a decimal point without a fraction digit (1.), an exponent without fraction digits (1.e2), and a missing integer part (-.5) are parse failures returning the DEAL null for a typed field and for a table-field string-keyed leaf — the emitted parser validates the strict RFC 8259 number grammar before Double.parseDouble, exactly like LuaJIT's std/json.lua parse_error (invalid number: leading zero not allowed / expected digit after decimal point) inside pcall(__json_parse, s), exit 0, never a throw — while valid spellings (42, 2.5, and a plain table-leaf number) still parse and validate

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-required-nodefault-defaults
tests.description: fromJson of a @jsonable class whose required fields carry NO declared default applies the reference defaults table: the per-type primitive zeroes (0 / 0.0 / false / ""), a FRESH empty table for a table field (toJson emits {} and a missing-key read yields the DEAL null), and a FRESH empty array for an array field (toJson emits [], .length reads 0, a past-end nullable read yields the DEAL null, and per-call freshness keeps a mutated instance's array separate from the next fromJson) — never a Java null crossing the non-nullable table/array boundary (the pre-fix emission crashed the first table read with a raw NullPointerException)

tests.name: jvm-jsonable-required-class-field-nodefault
tests.description: a required class-typed field with NO declared default: the reference defaults table holds a raw {} placeholder (a plain Lua table, never a class instance) which the typed Java slot cannot represent, so an ABSENT key is a fromJson validation failure (the DEAL null — the spec's never-throw contract; the pre-fix JVM silently read Java null at a typed read where LuaJIT's check_type raises E8001) while a PRESENT key deserializes the nested instance normally and its declared primitive fields keep the reference zeroes
